Threat.value: Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame
My body feels constantly tense and ready to react to danger
Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience

Memory.value: When I think about the frightening event I can sometimes smell things that I smelt when the frightening event happened.
When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

issues.explanation: 'Being naked' is hard to reconcile as a salient trigger for a life-threatening illness trauma unless there was a very specific exposure context; the other items point more toward nightmares/body sensations/illness-related reexperiencing, so this trigger appears poorly matched to the trauma type.

issues.item: Threat: Risky Behavior: Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
issues.explanation: Risk-taking is not well supported by the rest of the profile. The other threat and memory items describe fear, bodily alarm, pain, sensory recall, and dysregulated emotion rather than impulsive or reckless responding, so this item stands out as clinically disconnected.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Mistrust: People can't be trusted
issues.explanation: Global mistrust of other people is a weak fit with a primary trauma of life-threatening illness in the absence of any interpersonal betrayal, assault, or persecution content elsewhere in the profile. The rest of the appraisals are centered on bodily threat and fear of losing control, making this item comparatively incoherent.

vignette: Sami, a 38-year-old Middle Eastern man who works as a hairdresser in his community, has been struggling with significant distress following a life-threatening illness. The event left lasting scars both physically and mentally, manifesting in ways that have significantly impacted his daily life. Sami vividly remembers the day he was rushed to the hospital with severe pain. He recalls the sterile smell of antiseptics and the overwhelming fear as medical staff scrambled around him. This experience has left him extremely sensitive to triggers like related photos, waking up from nightmares, and undergoing any medical examination or procedure. When Sami sees a photo that reminds him of his illness, he immediately feels tense and ready to react to danger. His body's constant state of alertness amplifies the fear and horror he associates with those memories. One day, while looking at old pictures on social media, Sami saw an image from when he was hospitalized. The sight triggered a wave of negative emotions, plunging him into a deep sense of dread and panic. He felt his body tensing up, as if ready to flee or fight again. This reaction not only reinforced the trauma but also solidified his belief that his body is constantly on high alert, even when there's no real danger. The memories often resurface unexpectedly. For instance, the smell of antiseptics in the clinic during a routine check-up can transport Sami back to that hospital room, where he vividly remembers the pain and fear. When these memories come flooding back, they are accompanied by physical sensations such as the ache in his chest-a place where he felt intense discomfort during his illness. These experiences of reliving the event without clear images further intensify his feelings of vulnerability. Sami's negative appraisals compound his distress. He is certain that his body is betraying him and can no longer be trusted, which exacerbates his fear of going crazy. This belief makes every trigger more potent because he interprets these responses as signs of mental instability rather than normal reactions to trauma. For instance, when Sami smells antiseptics or sees related images, the memories return with a vengeance, intensifying his physical reactivity and negative emotions. Sami's fears have also affected his work as a hairdresser. He avoids handling any chemicals that might remind him of hospital environments, limiting his ability to use certain products in his salon. This has not only diminished his creativity but also led to some clients feeling like they are receiving subpar service. Despite this, Sami struggles to change his behavior because he is convinced that these precautions are necessary for his safety. The cycle of distress is relentless. When a memory or trigger resurfaces, the combination of negative emotions and physical reactivity confirms his belief that his body cannot be trusted, leading to heightened fear and further avoidance. This reinforcing loop has left Sami feeling increasingly isolated and distressed. What finally brought Sami to seek help was a particularly vivid nightmare that woke him up in the middle of the night, drenched in sweat and terrified. He realized that he could no longer function normally without some form of support. The worst part for him is the fear that he might never feel safe again, and he hopes therapy can provide him with tools to regain control over his life and body. Sami's story is one of persistent trauma echoes, where every trigger and memory reinforces a cycle of negative appraisals and heightened threat responses. His journey toward healing will require understanding these connections and developing strategies to break the reinforcing loop that has ensnared him.
